name: HackBench
creator: Meta, RAM team
measures: Whether an LLM monitor can find reward hacking in long agent trajectories
summary: Records from the same trajectory label the same commands differently, many inserted hacks cannot take effect, all 15 red-team records give the monitor the order to hack, and a string rule that reads nothing ties for third.
ranking: Cannot be re-checked: monitor settings and predictions are not released.

consistency: Published table ran on pre-release inputs
bias: Dataset builders are also ranked monitors

name: FrontierCS 2
creator: FrontierCS Team
measures: Whether an agent can rebuild a paper's key contribution and beat the authors' code
summary: Many tasks require beating the reference on every workload with no tolerance on noisy measurements, so even the reference often fails its own bar; one target is faster than any real reference run.
ranking: Model order mostly survives correction; pass-rate levels and close comparisons do not.

reviewability: Every task, judge and trace public
consistency: Pre- and post-fix scores mixed on 5 tasks
elicitation: Tight train-call budgets on some GPU tasks
bias: Effort and refusal handling differ by entry

name: DeepRSI
creator: Hillclimb
measures: Open-ended ML research engineering, ranked by Elo over per-task wins
summary: Rule-breaking attempts scored as valid, and disqualifications under a rule the prompt never states that change a task's winner.
ranking: Top four are robust under every correction; only the bottom two swap.

reviewability: Private verifier and held-out data not public
elicitation: GPT-6 Astra at 272k context, the Codex default
bias: One model on a different provider route

name: FrontierML
creator: Induction Labs
measures: Agentic ML engineering across 21 tasks, each run at three compute budgets
summary: Held-out data for every task sits in a public dataset the agents can reach, and 38 trials count with the rule-enforcing review skipped.
ranking: Robust: Opus 5.5 is first in every bootstrap replicate. Score levels are not.

reviewability: Graders, rubrics, anchors and trajectories public
scoring: 7/21 tasks, plus public held-out data for all 21
elicitation: Gemini 4 Argon hit provider quota errors
bias: The reviewer model is also a ranked model

name: AI4AI-Bench
creator: Einsia / Navers Lab
measures: Improving AI training recipes in real research repositories, scored against the shipped recipe
summary: A Sokoban test set the agent can rebuild in its own workspace, an image score that rewards pictures ignoring their prompts, an unlearning optimum above its metric's maximum, and checkpoints picked on the test set.
ranking: Opus 5 leads when averaged over efforts and is third at maximum effort only because of the Sokoban task; corrections move Kimi K3 to second.

reviewability: No patches or raw logs released
consistency: One protocol change, all cells rescored
bias: Unequal effort sets; first place unchanged

name: PostTrainBench
creator: aisa-group
measures: Agents post-training a small base model for one target benchmark in 10 hours on one H100
summary: No grading errors, and no reward hacks in the top run of each of its 24 tasks.

reviewability: 7 of 19 entries have no public runs
consistency: Small scorer commits a day after release
elicitation: Same GPU and time; native CLIs
